summary: The FSM Immigration Act says a permit is not required for a visit of 30 days or less; for a longer visit a permit may be issued for an additional period of up to 60 days, or, for citizens and nationals of the United States, the Marshall Islands and Palau, for the duration of the visit up to 365 days. The UK government says your passport must have an expiry date at least 120 days after the date you arrive, and that if you do not hold a valid entry permit you must complete a Customs, Immigration & Quarantine (CIQ) form on arrival.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says the currency is the US dollar, that most hotels accept credit cards and that ATM facilities are limited; Canada says there are few ATMs.
Canada's travel advice says to dress conservatively, behave discreetly and respect religious and social traditions. It also says drunkenness and drinking in public places are punishable offences.

Canada's travel advice says unexploded ordnance from World War II may pose a risk in certain areas: if you dive or boat, avoid doing so after daylight hours, avoid areas where sunken vessels or planes have been reported, and don't touch war remnants. It says it is illegal to remove anything from sunken World War II vessels or aircraft.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Micronesia?
faq.answer: Not for visits of 30 days or less: the FSM Immigration Act says no permit is required for them, and that for a longer visit a permit may be issued for an additional period of up to 60 days (up to 365 days for citizens and nationals of the United States, the Marshall Islands and Palau). The UK government says your passport must have an expiry date at least 120 days after the date you arrive, that without a valid entry permit you must complete a CIQ form on arrival, and that at border control you may need to show a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: What does the Compact of Free Association mean for US citizens?
faq.answer: The FSM Immigration Act says that, for citizens and nationals of the United States, for the effective period of the Compact of Free Association, a permit may be issued for the duration of the visit, not exceeding 365 days; no permit is required for a visit of 30 days or less.

faq.question: Can I stay longer than 30 days in Micronesia?
faq.answer: The FSM Immigration Act says a permit is not required for a visit of 30 days or less; for a visit in excess of 30 days a permit may be issued for an additional period not exceeding 60 days, or, for citizens and nationals of the United States (for the effective period of the Compact of Free Association), the Marshall Islands and Palau, for the duration of the visit, not exceeding 365 days.

faq.question: Do I need any vaccinations for Micronesia?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states a vaccination requirement for entering Micronesia.

entryRequirements.overstay.text: (1) Any person who, not being a citizen of the Federated States of Micronesia, unlawfully enters or attempts to enter the Federated States of Micronesia or having lawfully entered, remains willfully and unlawfully after expiration or revocation of his entry authorization, or who violates by act or omission any provision of this chapter or regulations issued pursuant thereto, upon conviction thereof shall be imprisoned for a period of not more than two years, or fined not more than $10,000, or both.

(2) In lieu of subsection (1) of this section or in addition thereto, any person who unlawfully enters the Federated States of Micronesia or having lawfully entered, willfully and unlawfully remains after expiration or revocation of his entry permit shall be subject to deportation after hearing upon application by the President or his designee to any competent court in the Federated States of Micronesia.
